title: Expl(AI)ned: The Impact of Explainable Artificial Intelligence on Users' Information Processing
authors: Bauer, K.; von Zahn, M.; Hinz, O.
tldr: Feature-based XAI explanations change users' situational information processing and mental models, but confirmation bias causes asymmetric adjustments that reinforce preconceptions while ignoring corrective explanations.
problem_and_motivation: Modern AI systems increasingly require explanations for their predictions due to regulations and transparency initiatives, yet how these explanations affect users' cognitive processes beyond trust and perception remains unstudied.
approach: Two incentivized experimental studies with complementary designs: Study 1 (n=607) with laypeople playing investment games, and Study 2 (n=153) with real estate experts predicting apartment listing prices.
Three-stage experimental design comparing baseline (no aid), opaque AI predictions, and XAI predictions with feature-based explanations (LIME in Study 1, SHAP in Study 2).
Between-subjects treatment design with difference-in-difference analysis to isolate explanation effects from prediction effects while controlling for individual-level fixed effects.
Study 1 used intentionally abstract investment game with 10 borrower characteristics designed to minimize participants' prior beliefs about feature-label relationships.
Study 2 used real apartment data from German online platforms with real estate industry professionals recruited through the Real Estate Association Germany (IVD).
Study 2 extended the design with four stages including a spillover test using apartments from a structurally different market (Chemnitz) to test domain transfer.
findings: num: 73.9% average absolute change in situational feature weighting when explanations were provided on top of predictions
num: 61.8% average absolute change in mental model coefficients after explanation exposure, persisting after explanations were removed
num: XAI participants decreased investment accuracy by 8.9% in Stage II and 9.6% in Stage III compared to opaque AI baseline
num: Mental model adjustments were approximately 50% larger when explanations confirmed prior beliefs versus conflicting with them
Opaque AI predictions alone did not cause significant mental model adjustments in either study, only explanations did

key_equations.explanation: Regression model measuring prediction and explanation effects on investment decisions.

key_equations.equation: Post_{ijk} = \beta_1 \cdot Pri_{ijk} + \beta_2 \cdot (AI_i \times Pri_{ijk}) + \beta_3 \cdot (Expl_i \times Pri_{ijk}) + \beta_4 \cdot SV_{ij} + \beta_5 \cdot (AI_i \times SV_{ij}) + \beta_6 \cdot (Expl_i \times SV_{ij}) + \gamma_i + \delta_k + \varepsilon
key_equations.explanation: Posterior belief formation model estimating prior belief stickiness and explanation pull.

definitions.definition: Explainable Artificial Intelligence - methods that present AI system predictions in understandable terms to humans.
Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations - perturbation-based method for generating local surrogate explanations of individual predictions.
SHapley Additive exPlanations - game-theoretic method for computing additive feature attributions to model predictions.
Cognitive representations encoding beliefs, facts, and knowledge that guide reasoning and decision-making.
Tendency to asymmetrically process information in ways that reinforce existing beliefs while discounting contradictory evidence.
Difference-in-difference - econometric method for isolating treatment effects by comparing pre-post changes between groups.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper identifies a novel cognitive mechanism through which feature-based XAI methods influence users' information processing and mental models beyond system perceptions.
directly_justifies: Feature-based explanations change users' situational weighting of available information in the direction of observed explanations.
Mental model adjustments from XAI are asymmetric: users reinforce confirming explanations but do not abandon disconfirming ones.
Opaque AI predictions alone do not cause significant mental model adjustments without accompanying explanations.
Explanation-driven mental model changes spill over to affect decision-making in unrelated domains by approximately 20%.
limits: The paper does not study personal finance systems or financial behavior directly; its findings on XAI and cognition are applicable but not specific to PFMS.
Study domains (investment games, real estate pricing) are not personal finance budgeting or spending contexts.
The paper does not evaluate budget recommendation, anomaly detection, or expense categorization algorithms relevant to PFMS.

limitations: No feedback on decision outcomes was provided, so effects under conditions of system performance feedback remain unknown.
Only local feature-based XAI methods (LIME and SHAP) were tested; other explanation forms may yield different cognitive effects.
Study 1 used deliberately abstract features unfamiliar to laypeople; effects with familiar, real-world features may differ.
The experimental setting prevented learning from experience; real-world repeated interaction with feedback could moderate documented effects.
Sample composition limits generalizability: Study 1 used Prolific crowdworkers; Study 2 used German real estate professionals only. [unacknowledged]
remember_this: Feature-based explanations cause both situational and lasting changes in how users process information.
Mental model adjustments from XAI are asymmetric due to confirmation bias, reinforcing preconceptions.
Opaque predictions alone do not cause significant mental model changes without explanations.
XAI explanation learning creates spillover effects altering decisions in unrelated domains by approximately 20 percent.
Decision performance decreased by 8.9 percent when users received explanations, driven by excessive reliance on confirming attributions.
